svg.text: MB102 supply · DSD TECH SH-U12 (RS-485) · SunFounder RC522 · Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47 · 1 kΩ/2 kΩ divider
SH-U12 TXD idles at 5 V; the ESP32-C6 is not
5 V tolerant. 1 kΩ in series from the TXD column,
2 kΩ down to ground, tap along row A to GP1.
Nothing else on the SH-U12 needs shifting.
A full-size board breaks each power rail in the middle.
The MB102 feeds the left halves only; the four 5 mm
jumpers at columns 30–32 carry 3.3 V, 5 V and both
grounds across. The tie at column 14 joins the grounds.
The wiki drawing is a bottom
view. Seen from above with the
and GP0–GP5 are the bottom row.
The kit is length-coded, not signal-coded — colour tells you which compartment to reach into, not what the wire carries. Check the code against your own box.
Each connection is one jumper. Solid core bends, so the runs go round the modules rather than through them; the colour is the length you need for the whole bent path, not the straight line.
Only the tamper switch and the RS-485 field wiring use flexible leads. Every other connection, the sounder included, is a jumper from the kit.
